newsitem.title: USA: US March S&P 500s roar higher, end near day's peak.
newsitem.headline: US March S&P 500s roar higher, end near day's peak.

text.p: U.S. March Standard and Poor's 500 futures roared higher late to end near a new session peak as bullishness gained momentum.
"It's the same old story," one S&P 500 floor source said. "If left alone, the market will just go higher."
Volume was heavy late, as a lack of news and no aggressive sellers helped extend Thursday's late recovery, they said.
The S&P floor source said five or six firms were buyers on the late rally that took March to a new session high of 757.60. Of those, they said Wall Street firms were big buyers.
"A lot of people were sitting on the sidelines (during the seasonal holidays) and now we're seeing money being put back in the market," one S&P trader said.
On Thursday, March S&Ps withstood a roller coaster session on the downside and closed above key 744.00, invigorating latent bulls early Friday.
Strength in Treasury bond futures and technology stocks rounded out the bullish environment for S&Ps, traders said.
"I think this market is just basically very sound," said Jay Hohmann, head futures trader for DLJ Securities in New York.
"But what we've seen this week is extremism that's negated itself day to day," Hohmann added.
"You can't help help but think that it's still kind of a seasonal mode, a holiday type of a thing," he said. "People are going to overreact."

March S&P 500s closed up more than 12 points on the day but still ended the week below Monday's session peak of 767.00. The 767.00 level is also the all-time high settlement set November 25, technicians said.
March S&Ps were resilient all session, even when March T-bonds came off their highs on strong U.S. data.

At settlement, March S&P 500s closed up 12.50 points to 757.20, Russell 2000s rose 3.00 points to 368.00, Value Line futures rallied 7.70 points to 692.70 and Nikkei 225 index futures rose 35.0 to 19,315.0. March Nasdaq 100 futures settled up 32.75 points to 858.75 after reaching a session high of 860.00, the highest price since December 20.
